sentences.zh: 而这次即兴表演里，我说了那段独白，而你只是痛苦地凝视着虚空，忍受着我的体味、我的近距离接触，还有我那故事的怪异感。

sentences.en: And it was, it was fantastic.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 他们当时是不是一直在给雷恩搭配不同的人？

sentences.en: You know that's the person when they're like, oh, let's see him with this person and this person and this person.
sentences.zh: 当他们说，哦，让我们看看他和这个人、那个人、还有那个人搭戏效果如何时，你就知道那个人就是最终人选了。

sentences.en: And like a ball.

sentences.en: Tiniest, tiniest little sprig.

sentences.en: Like, oh, we got to mix things up.

sentences.en: But Angela was furious.

sentences.zh: 安吉拉看了那一幕，气得不行。

sentences.en: Remember, they had me like look in the camera like they made me look so like they kept saying more anger, more.

sentences.en: I was like, oh, my God, my eyes are going to pop out of my head.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，天哪，我的眼珠都要瞪出来了。

sentences.zh: 但我认为，我认为我们的编剧当时只是坐在那儿。

sentences.zh: 我和珍娜讨论过这件事，我们也和编剧聊过。

sentences.en: how they would just take two names and put them on a card and just see what that felt like and sort of spitball a little bit about what those two people would bring out of each other.
sentences.zh: 他们会把两个名字写在卡片上，看看会有什么感觉，然后即兴探讨一下这两个人碰撞在一起会产生什么样的火花。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 这也是格雷格提到过的一点。

sentences.en: And I remember, and it's really great lesson for comedy writers and screenwriters.
sentences.zh: 我记得，这对喜剧编剧和剧本作家来说真的是一个很好的经验。

sentences.en: He said a lot of shows really focus on a character and like, oh, let's make this character really specific and funny and interesting.
sentences.zh: 他说很多剧集都专注于塑造一个角色，比如，哦，让我们把这个角色写得特别、有趣且引人入胜。

sentences.en: But he was really about like when these two two characters bang up against each other.
sentences.zh: 但他更看重的是当这两个角色发生碰撞时会怎样。

sentences.en: That's what she said.
Then what do what happens?
What happens with that energy?
sentences.zh: 那种能量会产生什么结果？

sentences.en: You know, so it was more about he was much more about dynamics between characters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他更关注的是角色之间的互动关系。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of the successes of the office.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是《办公室》成功的原因之一。

sentences.en: Well, this episode that we're talking about today, Golden Ticket, has a classic Michael Dwight pairing.
sentences.zh: 我们今天讨论的这一集《金奖券》，就有迈克尔和德怀特这对经典组合。

sentences.en: And we just I love in this rewatch watching the way that Dwight can be both Michael's lackey and then also like you can take him to task.
sentences.zh: 在这次重温中，我特别喜欢看德怀特如何既能当迈克尔的跟班，又能对他进行指责。

sentences.en: You stand up to him.
What was that like for you?
sentences.zh: 这对你来说是什么样的体验？

sentences.en: You were in this comedy duo with Steve Carell for seven years, playing out moments like this.
sentences.zh: 你和史蒂夫·卡瑞尔搭档了七年的喜剧二人组，演绎过很多这样的时刻。

sentences.en: What was that experience?
Well, that's a bunch of questions.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你这一连问了好几个问题。

sentences.en: And I know I that's how I like to interview people.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我采访别人时也喜欢这样。

sentences.en: She just likes to throw like 13 big, overarching, like huge questions all at once.
sentences.zh: 她就是喜欢一下子抛出十三个宏大、概括性的重磅问题。

sentences.en: I love it.
Well, let's let me hit that one.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我来回答那个问题。

sentences.en: Let me just say that, you know, when I look back on that work with Steve, I'm just so grateful because he's obviously like one of the greateSt.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，当我回首与史蒂夫共事的时光，我感到非常感激，因为他显然是史上最伟大的演员之一。

sentences.en: Actors, comedy actors, but even just actors like ever.
sentences.zh: 喜剧演员，甚至可以说是史上最伟大的演员之一。

sentences.en: And the fact that I got to do so much work with him was just such a gift.
sentences.zh: 能和他有那么多的合作，对我来说真是一份厚礼。

sentences.en: I didn't come from an improv background.
sentences.zh: 我并非出身于即兴表演背景。

sentences.en: I was always good at improv, but I went to theater school and I did Shakespeare and I did Eugene O'Neill.
sentences.zh: 我一直擅长即兴表演，但我上的是戏剧学校，演过莎士比亚和尤金·奥尼尔的作品。

sentences.en: And I was in New York kind of off off Broadway theater guy.
sentences.zh: 我以前在纽约是个演外外百老汇戏剧的演员。

sentences.en: And Steve was from Second City and had done years and years and years of improv.
sentences.zh: 而史蒂夫来自“第二城”剧团，有多年即兴表演的经验。

sentences.en: So that was his thing.

sentences.zh: 但关于史蒂夫，你知道，人们总是提到这一点。

sentences.en: It's kind of become a cliche, like the yes.
sentences.zh: 这已经成了一种陈词滥调，比如“是的，而且”。

sentences.en: And, you know, like an improv.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像在即兴表演中那样。

sentences.en: If you say like, hey, you know, I bought a pet peacock.
sentences.zh: 如果你说，嘿，我买了一只宠物孔雀。

sentences.en: Then you say yes.
And like, oh, I'd love to see it.
Can I feed it my mealworms or whatever?
sentences.zh: 我能喂它吃我的面包虫或者别的什么吗？

sentences.en: And Steve was incredible at that.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫在这方面简直太棒了。

sentences.en: No matter what I did.
And sometimes I would try to go really out of the box.
sentences.zh: 有时我会尝试跳出框架。

sentences.en: Steve would completely react in character and accept what was being proposed.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫会完全以角色的身份做出反应，并接受所提出的设定。

sentences.en: So I could just in the because obviously we would we would shoot a scene.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以在……因为显然我们会拍摄一场戏。

sentences.en: We would improvise.
I mean, we would do the script.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们会按照剧本演。

sentences.en: We would shoot the script and make sure we got it scripted correctly.
sentences.zh: 我们会拍摄剧本内容，确保剧本部分拍摄准确。

sentences.en: And then we would could improvise.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就可以进行即兴表演了。

sentences.en: And then sometimes it would just we just freely improvise and just go off.
sentences.zh: 有时我们甚至会完全自由地即兴发挥，随心所欲。

sentences.en: And I remember just being like I could say something like I decided to open a llama farm just out of nowhere or something.
sentences.zh: 我记得我当时会突然说些什么，比如我决定开一个羊驼农场，完全是突如其来的。

sentences.en: And Steve would just listen as Michael take that in and be like, wait, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫会以迈克尔的身份倾听，接受这个设定，然后说，等等，你在说什么？

sentences.en: Llamas?
What what does that have to do with anything?
sentences.zh: 这这跟那有什么关系吗？

sentences.en: Why?
You're so weird, Dwight.
Oh, go away.
You're icky.
Like and it would just be completely in the moment.
sentences.zh: 就像是完全沉浸在当下的那一刻。

sentences.en: And I just learned so much from that process.
sentences.zh: 而且我从那个过程中学到了很多。

sentences.en: He never got kind of like, God damn it, Rain.
sentences.zh: 他从来不会表现出那种“该死，雷恩”的感觉。

sentences.en: Why are you being so weird and so silly?
sentences.zh: 你为什么要表现得这么奇怪又这么傻？

sentences.en: Like stay on the point of the scene.
sentences.zh: 就像是紧扣场景的主题一样。

sentences.en: And we can go way off kilter, you know, way off the path.
sentences.zh: 我们可以偏离主题很远，你知道的，完全偏离轨道。

sentences.en: And he would just be right there all the time.
sentences.zh: 而他总是能一直待在那里。

sentences.en: It was really a privilege to work with him.
sentences.zh: 能和他一起工作真是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: I loved it when there'd be a conference room scene and clearly Michael had an agenda and things to say.
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢会议室的场景，迈克尔显然有自己的议程和想说的话。

sentences.en: And you you as Dwight, of all people, would interject.
sentences.zh: 而你，作为德怀特，竟然会插话。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.zh: 雷恩，我好多次去看剧本，想看看那是写好的还是即兴发挥的，因为我觉得我现在能分辨出来了。

sentences.en: And they're always so good.
sentences.zh: 而且它们总是那么精彩。

sentences.en: But but it's like seamless.
sentences.zh: 但这就像是天衣无缝的。

sentences.en: You would never know because of exactly what you just shared, because Steve is Michael.
sentences.zh: 你永远不会知道，就像你刚才分享的那样，因为史蒂夫就是迈克尔。

sentences.en: No matter what you piped up and said, just like would just take it and run with it.
sentences.zh: 无论你插嘴说了什么，他都能接住并顺着演下去。

sentences.en: And it was always like an absolute joy.
sentences.zh: 那真是一种绝对的乐趣。

sentences.en: You know me.
I'm a nerdy, nerdy improv gal.
sentences.zh: 我是一个书呆子式的即兴表演爱好者。

sentences.en: Well, we've talked on the podcast that you and Jenna had your whole like we did theater.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在播客里聊过，你和珍娜你们俩有那种“我们演过戏”的经历。

sentences.en: And Jenna likes to remind me of it, Rain, much like you did.
sentences.zh: 珍娜喜欢提醒我这一点，雷恩，就像你刚才做的那样。

sentences.en: But as like a nerdy improv gal watching you guys, it was it was just awesome.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个看着你们表演的书呆子即兴爱好者，这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: I felt like I had a front row seat of just some really magical moments.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己就像坐在前排，亲眼见证了一些真正神奇的时刻。

sentences.en: And getting specifically to Golden Ticket.
sentences.zh: 专门说到《金奖券》这一集。

sentences.en: Thank you, Angela.

sentences.zh: 而且，是的，自从这一集播出后我就没再看过。

sentences.zh: 珍娜，就像你说的，德怀特那种马屁精、走狗、奉承者的动态，是那么渴望得到迈克尔的认可。

sentences.en: And then oddly, realizing he's got some power here.
sentences.zh: 然后奇怪的是，他意识到自己在这里也有了一些权力。

sentences.en: And, you know, that switch when he's shaking David Wallace's hand and he says, you know, thank you and takes the credit for it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当他握住大卫·华莱士的手说“谢谢你”并把功劳揽到自己身上时，那种转变。

sentences.en: And then Steve's expression of it was so priceless of like, oh, that guy.
sentences.zh: 还有史蒂夫当时那种无价的表情，仿佛在说“噢，这家伙”。

sentences.en: And then your fight in the marketing meeting, like when you get on the phone with the marketing guys, the two of you back and forth with your big ideas.
sentences.zh: 还有你们在营销会议上的争吵，比如当你和营销人员通电话时，你们俩来回抛出那些宏大的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah, horse boats and all the toilet, toilet, toilet net is a lot of toilet ideas.

sentences.zh: 还有一两件其他东西，我记不太清了。

sentences.en: blah, blah.
